families.title: Choose the answer

mistakeCategories.description: Picked a term with a related but different meaning.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Close, but that one means something different. Compare the two meanings side by side, then try again.

mistakeCategories.description: Picked the opposite meaning (e.g. louder for quieter).
mistakeCategories.feedback: That's the opposite direction. Look again at which way the music should change.

mistakeCategories.description: Picked an answer from a different category (e.g. a tempo word for a dynamic).
mistakeCategories.feedback: That answer belongs to a different kind of instruction. Ask yourself: is this about speed, volume, or how the notes are played?

families.correctFeedback: Correct — and you can explain why.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Read the explanation, then try a similar question.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Options are a native list of buttons with full text labels; any music shown has a text description.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Note and rest values

mistakeCategories.description: Chose a value twice or half as long as the target.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That value is twice (or half) as long. Count it in crotchet beats and compare.

mistakeCategories.description: Ignored or mis-added a dot.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Remember: a dot adds half of the note's own value. Work out that half, then add it.

mistakeCategories.description: Confused a note with its matching rest, or two similar-looking rests.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check the shape carefully. A rest that hangs below its line lasts longer than one that sits on top of it.

mistakeCategories.description: Treated a tie or a dot incorrectly when totalling.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A tie joins two notes into one sound, so add both values together.

mistakeCategories.description: Counted tuplet notes at their written value.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Those notes are a tuplet, so they share a different amount of time. Look at the number written over them.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — those durations match exactly.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Try counting each value in crotchet beats.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Values are announced by name and length in beats; the rhythm can be stepped through note by note with the keyboard.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Build a bar

mistakeCategories.description: Too many beats for the time signature.
mistakeCategories.feedback: This bar holds more beats than the time signature allows. Count the beats again and remove the extra.

mistakeCategories.description: Too few beats for the time signature.
mistakeCategories.feedback: There's still room in this bar. Count how many beats are missing.

mistakeCategories.description: Grouping hides where a beat begins.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The beats add up, but it's hard to see where each beat starts. Regroup the notes so every beat is visible.

mistakeCategories.description: A tie is used where one note value would do.
mistakeCategories.feedback: You can write those tied notes as a single note (or a dotted note). That's easier to read.

mistakeCategories.description: Rests are not grouped by beat.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Each silent beat (or part-beat) normally gets its own rest. Split the silence along the beats.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — the bar is complete and easy to read.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Check the beat total first, then how the notes are grouped.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Each slot is a labelled list position; the learner adds values from a named palette and hears or reads the running beat total.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Time signature

mistakeCategories.description: Wrong number of beats per bar.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Count the beats in one complete bar again — that gives the top number.

mistakeCategories.description: Right number of beats but wrong beat value.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The beat count is right, but what kind of note is each beat? That gives the bottom number.

mistakeCategories.description: Confused simple and compound time.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Do the beats split into two or into three? Two means simple time; three means compound.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — the beats and beat value both match.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Find the beat first, then count how many fit in a bar.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: The rhythm is presented as a text list of values per bar with beat markers.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Add the bar-lines

mistakeCategories.description: A bar contains too many beats.
mistakeCategories.feedback: One of your bars holds too many beats. Count from the last bar-line.

mistakeCategories.description: A bar contains too few beats.
mistakeCategories.feedback: One of your bars is short. Count from the last bar-line.

mistakeCategories.description: Forgot the final double bar-line.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Music ends with a double bar-line — add it at the very end.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — every bar has the right number of beats.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Count beats from the start, bar by bar.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: The learner moves through gaps between notes with arrow keys and toggles a bar-line; running totals are announced.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Group notes and rests

mistakeCategories.description: Beamed across the middle of a four-beat bar.
mistakeCategories.feedback: In four-beat bars, keep the two halves of the bar visible — don't beam across the middle.

mistakeCategories.description: A single rest covers parts of two beats.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That rest hides where a beat begins. Use one rest to finish the beat, and another for the next.

mistakeCategories.description: A two-beat rest is placed in the middle of a four-beat bar.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A two-beat rest can fill the first or second half of a four-beat bar, but not the middle two beats.

mistakeCategories.description: Used a tie inside a beat where a dotted note is clearer.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A dotted note says the same thing more simply here.

mistakeCategories.description: In compound time the dotted beat is hidden by the grouping.
mistakeCategories.feedback: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — the grouping shows every beat clearly.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Mark where each beat starts, then regroup.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Beams and rests are listed per beat; the learner chooses a grouping option for each beat from a list.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Tuplets

mistakeCategories.description: The tuplet group does not fill the intended time.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A tuplet still fills a fixed amount of time. Check which beat it replaces.

mistakeCategories.description: Wrong tuplet number.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Count the notes that share the beat — that's the number to write over the group.

mistakeCategories.description: Notes written with the wrong value or number of beams.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Use the note value the group would have if it divided normally — then add the tuplet number.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — the group fits the beat exactly.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Ask: how many notes, in the time of how many?

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Tuplet groups are described as 'n notes in the time of m'; values are chosen from a list.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Read a note

mistakeCategories.description: Read a line note as a space note or vice versa.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Look closely: is the line running through the note-head, or is the note sitting between two lines?

mistakeCategories.description: Read the note as if in a different clef.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That would be right in another clef. Check the clef at the start of the stave first.

mistakeCategories.description: Counted lines or spaces from the top instead of the bottom.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Lines and spaces are counted from the bottom of the stave upwards.

mistakeCategories.description: Answered the letter name one step away.
mistakeCategories.feedback: You're one step away. Find a note you know for certain and count up or down from it.

mistakeCategories.description: Miscounted ledger lines.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Count the ledger lines one at a time, from the stave outwards.

mistakeCategories.description: Ignored an accidental or key signature.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The letter is right, but check for a sharp, flat or natural — in the key signature or in front of the note.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — you read that note accurately.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Start from the clef and count from a note you know.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Each note is reachable with arrow keys and announced as clef, line/space number and ledger lines; answers are typed or picked from letter buttons.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Write a note

mistakeCategories.description: Correct letter in the wrong octave.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That's the right letter name, but in a different octave. Check which one the question asks for.

mistakeCategories.description: Placed on a line instead of a space or vice versa.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Nearly — move it between a line and a space and check again.

mistakeCategories.description: Placed as if in a different clef.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That position would be right in a different clef. Look at the clef first.

mistakeCategories.description: Wrong number of ledger lines.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Count the ledger lines needed — one for each line above or below the stave.

mistakeCategories.description: Counted lines or spaces from the top instead of the bottom.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Lines and spaces are counted from the bottom of the stave upwards.

mistakeCategories.description: Required accidental missing or wrong.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The position is right, but the note needs its sharp, flat or natural.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — that note is in exactly the right place.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Find a reference note and count lines and spaces from it.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Up/down arrow keys move a cursor through staff positions with announced pitch names; accidentals are toggled with keys.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Find it on the keyboard

mistakeCategories.description: Pressed a neighbouring white key.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Close — you're one white key away. Use the groups of two and three black keys to find your place.

mistakeCategories.description: Pressed the black key on the wrong side.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Sharps are just to the right; flats are just to the left.

mistakeCategories.description: Right key, but the task asks for a particular spelling.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That key is right, but here the note needs a different name. Think about which letter the question asks for.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — that's the key.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Find the nearest group of black keys and count from there.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Keys are buttons in pitch order announced by name; the learner can type a letter name instead of pressing a key.
accessibility.withoutSound: Sound is optional reinforcement only.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Which note sounds?

mistakeCategories.description: Forgot that an accidental lasts for the rest of the bar.
mistakeCategories.feedback: An accidental keeps working for the rest of the bar on that line or space.

mistakeCategories.description: Carried an accidental into the next bar.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A bar-line cancels accidentals — unless the note is tied across it.

mistakeCategories.description: Ignored the key signature.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Don't forget the key signature: it affects every note with that letter name.

mistakeCategories.description: Applied an accidental to the same letter in a different octave.
mistakeCategories.feedback: An accidental only affects notes on the same line or space — not the same letter in another octave.

mistakeCategories.description: Missed that a tie carries the accidental over the bar-line.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A tie carries the accidental into the next bar, but only for the tied note.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — you tracked the accidentals perfectly.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Go through the bar from the start, tracking each accidental.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Bars are read note by note with the active key signature and accidental state announced.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Build a scale

mistakeCategories.description: Tones and semitones are in the wrong places.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check the pattern of tones and semitones — the semitones aren't where they belong.

mistakeCategories.description: A letter name is skipped or used twice (enharmonic spelling).
mistakeCategories.feedback: Each letter name appears once. You've used one letter twice and skipped another — respell that note.

mistakeCategories.description: Used the wrong minor form.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check which form of the minor scale is asked for, and which notes that form changes.

mistakeCategories.description: Melodic minor descending still has raised 6th/7th.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Coming down, the melodic minor uses the notes of the key signature — undo the raised 6th and 7th.

mistakeCategories.description: Key signature wrong, or accidentals duplicated alongside it.
mistakeCategories.feedback: With a key signature, notes it covers don't need accidentals. Without one, every sharp or flat must be written.

mistakeCategories.description: Scale written in the wrong direction or octave.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check whether the question asks for ascending or descending, and which octave to start on.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — every note is spelt and placed correctly.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Write one note per letter name first, then check the tones and semitones.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: The scale is built note by note from letter and accidental pickers; each choice and the interval from the previous note are announced.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Key signatures and keys

mistakeCategories.description: Wrong number of sharps/flats.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Count again: each key has a fixed number of sharps or flats.

mistakeCategories.description: Sharps/flats in the wrong order.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Key signatures always follow the same order. Check which comes first.

mistakeCategories.description: Correct accidentals in the wrong positions for the clef.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The accidentals are right, but some are on the wrong line or space for this clef.

mistakeCategories.description: Confused a key with its relative major/minor.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That key shares this key signature, but it's the relative key. Check the tonic.

mistakeCategories.description: Mixed sharps and flats.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A key signature uses only sharps or only flats.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — that key signature is exactly right.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Recall the order of sharps or flats and count how many the key needs.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Accidentals are added from a list; their positions are announced as line/space names in the current clef.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Scale degrees

mistakeCategories.description: Counted degrees from a note other than the tonic.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Count from the tonic (the key note) as degree 1.

mistakeCategories.description: Counted the starting note as 0.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The tonic itself is degree 1 — count it too.

mistakeCategories.description: Matched the wrong technical name to a degree.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check the technical name that belongs to that degree number.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — that's the right degree.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Write out the scale from the tonic and count.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Notes and options are announced in text.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Intervals

mistakeCategories.description: Interval number off by one (did not count both notes).
mistakeCategories.feedback: Count both notes: the bottom note is 1, then every letter name up to and including the top note.

mistakeCategories.description: Quality judged from the wrong key or scale.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Judge the quality by imagining the major scale on the lower note. Is the top note in it?

mistakeCategories.description: Added 8 instead of 7 for a compound interval.
mistakeCategories.feedback: An octave plus a 5th is a 12th, not a 13th: the shared note is counted only once.

mistakeCategories.description: Built the right sound with the wrong letter name.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That sounds right, but intervals depend on letter names. Check how many letter names the interval spans.

mistakeCategories.description: Confused augmented with diminished (or major with minor).
mistakeCategories.feedback: Is the interval a semitone bigger or smaller than the major/perfect version? Bigger means augmented; smaller means diminished (or minor).

families.correctFeedback: Correct — number and quality both match.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Count the letter names first, then compare with the major scale on the lower note.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Both notes are announced by name; build tasks use letter/accidental pickers.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Triads and chords

mistakeCategories.description: Identified the wrong scale degree as the root.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Find the root: rearrange the notes into stacked 3rds — the lowest note of that stack is the root.

mistakeCategories.description: Assumed the bass note is always the root.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The lowest note isn't always the root. Stack the notes in 3rds to find it, then check the inversion.

mistakeCategories.description: Wrong inversion letter or figures.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Inversion depends on which note of the triad is in the bass: root (a), 3rd (b) or 5th (c).

mistakeCategories.description: In a minor key, missed the raised leading note.
mistakeCategories.feedback: In minor keys, chords use the harmonic minor, so the leading note is raised.

mistakeCategories.description: A triad note is missing or wrong.
mistakeCategories.feedback: One of the notes doesn't belong. A triad has a root, a 3rd and a 5th.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — right chord and right position.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Find the root first, then the bass note.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Chord notes are listed from the bass upward by name; answers are picked from labelled options.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Cadences

mistakeCategories.description: Chosen chord does not contain the melody note.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The chord must include the melody note above it. Check the notes of the chord you chose.

mistakeCategories.description: The two chords do not form a perfect, plagal or imperfect cadence.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Those two chords don't make one of the cadences. A cadence ends on chord I or chord V.

mistakeCategories.description: The cadence is named incorrectly.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Look at the second chord: ending on V makes an imperfect cadence; V–I is perfect; IV–I is plagal.

mistakeCategories.description: Chords chosen in the wrong key.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check the key signature and the final note — then build the chords in that key.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — those chords fit the melody and make the cadence.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. For each marked note, list the chords that contain it, then choose a pair that makes a cadence.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Melody notes and chord options are listed by name; chord choices are made from labelled buttons; cadence names from a list.
accessibility.withoutSound: Sound playback of the cadence is optional and has an equivalent text description.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Transpose

mistakeCategories.description: Melody written in the wrong octave (or same pitch).
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check the octave: the new version should be exactly one octave higher or lower — not the same pitch, and not two octaves away.

mistakeCategories.description: Used the wrong clef (e.g. alto instead of tenor).
mistakeCategories.feedback: Look at which clef the question asks for — alto and tenor clefs are easy to mix up.

mistakeCategories.description: Transposed by the wrong interval.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check the interval given in the question, and count letter names as well as semitones.

mistakeCategories.description: Transposed in the wrong direction (written ↔ concert).
mistakeCategories.feedback: Think about the instrument: a B♭ instrument sounds lower than written, so written notes are higher than concert pitch.

mistakeCategories.description: New key signature missing or wrong.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Work out the new key first and write its key signature.

mistakeCategories.description: Copied an accidental instead of transposing it.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Accidentals change too. Work out what each altered note is in the original key, then find the same degree in the new key.

mistakeCategories.description: Right sound, wrong spelling.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That sounds right, but the spelling is wrong. Keep each note the same interval number above its original.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — every note is transposed, spelt and placed correctly.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Transpose the key first, then each note, then check accidentals.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Source notes are listed by name; the answer is entered note by note with letter/accidental/octave pickers.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Chromatic scale

mistakeCategories.description: A letter name is used three times.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Each letter name can appear at most twice in a chromatic scale.

mistakeCategories.description: A letter name is missing.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Every letter name must appear at least once.

mistakeCategories.description: Steps that are not semitones.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Every step in a chromatic scale is a semitone. Check where the gap is bigger.

mistakeCategories.description: Spelling that ignores the key signature and adds needless accidentals.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That's correct but harder to read. With this key signature, choose spellings that need fewer accidentals.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — a clear, correctly spelt chromatic scale.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Check that each step is a semitone and each letter appears once or twice.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Built note by note with letter/accidental pickers; semitone steps are announced.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Enharmonic equivalents

mistakeCategories.description: Gave the same spelling instead of a different one.
mistakeCategories.feedback: The question asks for a different name for the same sound.

mistakeCategories.description: Gave a note that sounds different.
mistakeCategories.feedback: That note sounds at a different pitch. An enharmonic equivalent must sound exactly the same.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — same sound, different spelling.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Find the key on the keyboard, then list every name it can have.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Keys and spellings are announced in text.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Ornaments

mistakeCategories.description: Confused upper and lower mordent.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Check the direction: the upper mordent goes up to the note above; the lower mordent goes down to the note below.

mistakeCategories.description: Confused a turn with an inverted turn.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A turn starts on the note above; an inverted turn starts on the note below.

mistakeCategories.description: Confused acciaccatura and appoggiatura.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Look for the slash through the small note: with it, the note is crushed in quickly (acciaccatura); without it, it takes time from the main note (appoggiatura).

mistakeCategories.description: Confused a trill with a mordent.
mistakeCategories.feedback: A trill keeps alternating for the length of the note; a mordent is just one quick alternation.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — that's the right ornament.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Compare the shape of the sign with each ornament's pattern.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: Signs are described in words and the written-out figures are listed note by note.
accessibility.withoutSound: Optional audio examples have text descriptions.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.

families.title: Questions on a score

mistakeCategories.description: Misread the relevant bar/note in the score.
mistakeCategories.feedback: Look again at the bar the question points to — find the exact note or sign first.

mistakeCategories.description: Applied the right idea in the wrong way.
mistakeCategories.feedback: You found the right place, but check the rule you used — see the hint for that part.

families.correctFeedback: Correct — you read the score carefully and applied the theory.
families.fallbackFeedback: Not quite. Find the bar the question mentions, then answer one part at a time.

accessibility.screenReaderEquivalent: The score is navigable bar by bar and note by note with a full text description; each sub-question is a standard accessible widget.
accessibility.withoutSound: All information is visual or textual; no sound is required.
accessibility.withoutColour: Correctness is shown with icons and text as well as colour.
